claim.quote: A large asymmetry with a sin(phi) modulation is observed, as predicted for the interference term of Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering and the Bethe-Heitler process.

key_value.note: Amplitude of the sin(phi) modulation, as stated in the abstract.
key_value.quote: The amplitude of this modulation is alpha = 0.202 +/- 0.028.

name: CLAS observation of exclusive DVCS beam-spin asymmetry
notes: Result type follows the title wording "Observation of exclusive DVCS ...".

summary.plain: CLAS measured how often electrons of opposite spin orientation scatter from protons while radiating a photon. A large, predicted angular modulation showed that deeply virtual Compton scattering, a probe of the proton's internal structure, could be studied at Jefferson Lab.
summary.technical: First CLAS measurement of the beam-spin asymmetry in ep→epγ at 4.25 GeV: a large sin(φ) asymmetry from DVCS-Bethe-Heitler interference, with modulation amplitude α = 0.202 ± 0.028, directly proportional to the imaginary part of the DVCS amplitude at leading order and leading twist.

title: Observation of exclusive DVCS in polarized electron beam asymmetry measurements
why_it_matters: DVCS gives access to generalised parton distributions, which describe the three-dimensional structure of the nucleon; this was an early demonstration at JLab energies.
